newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEPs mourn death of British Socialist Ken Stewart.
newsitem.headline: MEPs mourn death of British Socialist Ken Stewart.

text.p: British Socialist MEP Ken Stewart, a champion of safety at sea, died on Monday at the age of 69. He had suffered from diabetes for some time.

"Ken Stewart's loss to the European Parliament and the Labour Group is immense. He brought a wealth of valuable experience and knowledge to his work as an MEP," the leader of the European Parliamentary Labour Party, Wayne David, said in a statement on Tuesday.
A by-election will have to be held in Stewart's Merseyside West constituency before next March, to replace the MEP who represented the area for the last 12 years.
Britain, which is due to hold a general election before mid-May 1997, is the only European Union member where MEPs are elected individually.
Voters in other member states select a list of candidates put up by a political party. When an MEP's seat becomes vacant, it is filled by another person from the same list.

Stewart, a Liverpool City Councillor since 1964, was an active member of the parliament's transport committee and a vocal advocate of safety improvements on roll-on roll-off ferries and other vessels.
Fellow Euro-MPs are expected to make a tribute to the former carpenter/joiner at the start of the parliament's plenary session in Brussels on September 4.
